newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, blue chips firmer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, blue chips firmer.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Monday after a quiet trading session with selected blue chips leading the gainers.
Dealers said investors were mostly sidelined, unsure of the near-term direction of Wall Street stocks and its impact.

"There was some light bargain hunting in selected stocks and Singapore banks. But the banks have moved up quite a bit and I'll be quite neutral at these levels," said a broker with a local firm. Foreign tranches of DBS, OCBC and OUB ended higher by between S$0.50 and S$0.20 each in moderately active trading.
The Straits Times Industrial Index ended up 12.36 points at 2,088.14. The UOB OTC index, tracking mostly Malaysian shares traded over the counter, fell 5.88 points to 1,218.20.
Total market volume was 112.62 million shares with 174 gainers matching 174 losers.
Sentiment for Malaysian OTC stocks continued to be weak after the central bank imposed curbs on property and stocks lending, Dealers said.
HongKong Land Holdings topped the actives list with over four million traded and ended down seven cents at US$2.31. NatSteel was also active and closed six cents higher at S$3.62.
